chapter_text:
CHAPTER 18 - CONSTRUCTIONS

Introduction

Geometry is not only about proving results; it is also about DRAWING accurate figures. In this chapter we use only two instruments - a RULER (a straight edge marked in centimetres) and a pair of COMPASSES - to construct figures precisely. These are called RULER-AND-COMPASS constructions. A construction is different from a rough sketch: every point and line is obtained by a definite sequence of steps, and each step can be justified using the congruence and circle theorems learned earlier. We also use a protractor and set-squares only to CHECK our work, never to make the actual construction, because the aim is to build the figure from first principles.

18.1 BISECTING A LINE SEGMENT (PERPENDICULAR BISECTOR)

To bisect a given line segment AB means to find its mid-point and to draw the line that cuts it into two equal halves at right angles.
Steps of construction:
 1. With A as centre and radius more than half of AB, draw arcs on both sides of AB.
 2. With B as centre and the SAME radius, draw two more arcs cutting the first pair at points P (above AB) and Q (below AB).
 3. Join P and Q. The line PQ meets AB at M. Then M is the mid-point of AB and PQ is perpendicular to AB.
Justification: Because equal radii were used, AP = BP = AQ = BQ. Points P and Q are therefore each equidistant from A and B, so both lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB. The line joining two points equidistant from the ends of a segment is exactly the perpendicular bisector, so PQ is the perpendicular bisector and M is the mid-point. To construct only the PERPENDICULAR to a line AT a given point, or FROM a point to a line, the same equidistant idea is used.

18.2 BISECTING AN ANGLE

To bisect a given angle ABC means to draw a ray from the vertex B that divides the angle into two equal parts.
Steps of construction:
 1. With B as centre and any convenient radius, draw an arc that cuts BA at P and BC at Q.
 2. With P as centre and a radius more than half of PQ, draw an arc in the interior of the angle.
 3. With Q as centre and the same radius, draw another arc cutting the previous one at R.
 4. Join B and R. The ray BR is the required bisector, so angle ABR = angle RBC.
Justification: BP = BQ (same radius) and PR = QR (same radius). BR is common to triangles BPR and BQR, so by the SSS criterion the two triangles are congruent, giving angle PBR = angle QBR. Hence BR bisects the angle.

18.3 CONSTRUCTING STANDARD ANGLES

Certain angles can be made exactly with ruler and compasses.
Constructing 60°: Draw a ray BC. With B as centre and any radius draw an arc cutting BC at Q. With Q as centre and the same radius, cut the first arc at R. Join BR. Then angle RBC = 60°. This works because BQ = QR = BR forms an equilateral triangle, and each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.
Constructing 120°: Repeat the 60° step once more - from R, with the same radius, cut the arc again at S and join BS; angle SBC = 120° (two 60° arcs placed side by side).
Constructing 30°: First construct 60° as above, then BISECT it. Half of 60° is 30°.
Constructing 90°: Construct 60° and 120° on the same arc (points R and S), then bisect the angle between them. Since the bisector of the 60°-to-120° gap lies at 90° from BC, angle at B = 90°. Equivalently, erect a perpendicular to BC at B.
Constructing 45°: First construct 90°, then bisect it. Half of 90° is 45°.
By repeatedly bisecting, further angles such as 15°, 22.5°, 75° and 105° can be obtained - for example 75° is the bisector of the 60°-90° gap, and 105° = 60° + 45°.

18.4 CONSTRUCTION OF TRIANGLES

A triangle can be constructed uniquely when enough independent measurements are given. The usual cases correspond to the congruence conditions.
(a) Three sides given (SSS): To construct triangle ABC with BC = a, CA = b, AB = c. Draw base BC = a. With B as centre and radius c draw an arc; with C as centre and radius b draw another arc cutting the first at A. Join AB and AC. (Possible only if the sum of any two sides is greater than the third - the triangle inequality.)
(b) Two sides and the included angle (SAS): To construct triangle ABC with BC = a, angle B, and AB = c. Draw base BC = a. At B construct the given angle. Along that arm mark off BA = c. Join AC.
(c) Two angles and the included side (ASA): To construct triangle ABC with BC = a, angle B and angle C. Draw base BC = a. At B construct angle B and at C construct angle C. The two arms meet at A. (If instead two angles and a NON-included side are given, first find the third angle using the angle-sum property, then use ASA.)
(d) Base, a base angle and the SUM of the other two sides: To construct triangle ABC given BC = a, angle B, and AB + AC = s. Draw BC = a. At B construct the given angle and along its arm mark BD = s (the whole sum). Join DC. Draw the perpendicular bisector of DC; it meets BD at A. Then triangle ABC is required. Justification: A lies on the perpendicular bisector of DC, so AD = AC. Hence AB + AC = AB + AD = BD = s, as required.
(e) Base, a base angle and the DIFFERENCE of the other two sides: given BC = a, angle B, and AB - AC (or AC - AB). Draw BC and construct angle B. If AB - AC is given (AB the longer), mark BD = AB - AC along the arm; join DC and draw the perpendicular bisector of DC to meet the arm at A. Then AD = AC and AB - AC = BD. (If AC - AB is given, D is taken on the opposite side of B along the arm produced.)
(f) Right triangle given the hypotenuse and one side (RHS): To construct a right triangle with the right angle at B, one side BC = a, and hypotenuse AC = h. Draw BC = a. At B erect a perpendicular. With C as centre and radius h draw an arc cutting the perpendicular at A. Join AC. Then angle B = 90° and AC = h.

18.5 DIVIDING A LINE SEGMENT IN A GIVEN RATIO

To divide a segment AB internally in the ratio m : n (m and n whole numbers):
Steps of construction:
 1. Draw AB. From A draw any ray AX making an acute angle with AB.
 2. Along AX mark off (m + n) equal segments AA1, A1A2, ..., using the compasses with a fixed opening, so the points A1, A2, ..., A(m+n) are equally spaced.
 3. Join the LAST point A(m+n) to B.
 4. Through the point Am (the m-th point from A), draw a line PARALLEL to A(m+n)B, meeting AB at P.
 5. Then P divides AB so that AP : PB = m : n.
Justification: The equal spacing on AX and the parallel lines create similar triangles (Basic Proportionality / Thales theorem). Because Am is the m-th of the (m + n) equal parts and the parallel line cuts AB proportionally, AP : PB = Am-parts : remaining-parts = m : n.

18.6 CONSTRUCTING A TRIANGLE SIMILAR TO A GIVEN TRIANGLE (SCALE FACTOR)

Given triangle ABC, we construct a similar triangle whose sides are in a given ratio (scale factor) k = p/q to the corresponding sides of ABC.
Case scale factor less than 1 (e.g. 2/3):
 1. Draw the given triangle ABC. Below BC (on the opposite side to A) draw a ray BX making an acute angle with BC.
 2. Mark off q equal points B1, B2, ..., Bq on BX (here q = 3).
 3. Join Bq (the last point, B3) to C.
 4. Through Bp (the p-th point, B2) draw a line parallel to BqC meeting BC at C'.
 5. Through C' draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at A'. Triangle A'BC' is similar to ABC with each side (2/3) of the original.
Case scale factor greater than 1 (e.g. 5/3): mark the LARGER of p and q points (5 points) on BX, join the q-th point (B3) to C, then through the p-th point (B5) draw a line parallel to B3C meeting BC PRODUCED at C', and continue as before; the new triangle is larger than ABC.
Justification: The equally spaced points and parallels again set up the Basic Proportionality Theorem, forcing BC' : BC = p : q and giving triangle A'BC' similar to ABC (AA similarity, since corresponding sides are parallel and angles equal).

18.7 CONSTRUCTING TANGENTS TO A CIRCLE

A tangent to a circle touches it at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
Tangent at a point on the circle: Given circle with centre O and a point P on it, join OP and construct the perpendicular to OP at P. That perpendicular is the required tangent, because the tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.
Tangents from an external point: Given a circle with centre O and a point A outside it, two tangents can be drawn.
Steps of construction:
 1. Join OA and find its mid-point M (by drawing the perpendicular bisector of OA).
 2. With M as centre and radius MO (= MA), draw a circle. It cuts the given circle at two points P and Q.
 3. Join AP and AQ. These are the two required tangents.
Justification: OA is a diameter of the new circle, and any angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle OPA = angle OQA = 90°. Thus AP is perpendicular to the radius OP at P (and AQ to OQ at Q), which means AP and AQ touch the circle - they are tangents. The two tangents from an external point are always equal in length (AP = AQ).

SUMMARY

- Ruler-and-compass constructions use only a straight edge and compasses; a protractor is used only to verify.
- To bisect a segment, draw equal arcs from both ends and join their intersections; this gives the perpendicular bisector through the mid-point.
- To bisect an angle, cut equal arcs on the two arms and from those cut equal arcs meeting at a point; the ray from the vertex to that point is the bisector (justified by SSS congruence).
- 60° comes from an equilateral-triangle arc; 120° from two such arcs; 30°, 45°, 90° come by bisecting 60°, 90° and by erecting perpendiculars.
- Triangles are constructed from SSS, SAS or ASA data; special cases use the perpendicular bisector when the SUM or DIFFERENCE of two sides is given, and the RHS case for right triangles.
- A segment is divided in ratio m : n by marking (m + n) equal parts on an auxiliary ray and drawing a parallel - a use of the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
- A similar triangle with scale factor p/q is built with the same auxiliary-ray-and-parallel idea; p > q enlarges, p < q reduces.
- Tangents from an external point A are found by drawing the circle on OA as diameter; it meets the given circle at the points of contact, and the tangents are equal in length.

topics.name: Basic Constructions (Bisectors)
topics.description: Bisecting a line segment to obtain its perpendicular bisector and mid-point; erecting perpendiculars; the equidistant-point justification using congruent triangles.

topics.name: Construction of Standard Angles
topics.description: Bisecting an angle and constructing standard angles 60°, 120°, 30°, 90°, 45° (and combinations like 75°, 105°, 15°) using equilateral-triangle arcs and repeated bisection.

topics.name: Construction of Triangles
topics.description: Constructing triangles from SSS, SAS and ASA data, and the special cases: base with a base angle and the sum or difference of the other two sides, and the RHS right-triangle case (hypotenuse and one side).

topics.name: Dividing a Segment in a Ratio
topics.description: Dividing a given line segment internally in a ratio m : n using an auxiliary ray with equal marks and a parallel line, justified by the Basic Proportionality (Thales) Theorem.

topics.name: Constructing Similar Triangles (Scale Factor)
topics.description: Constructing a triangle similar to a given triangle for a scale factor p/q, both for reduction (p < q) and enlargement (p > q), using equally-spaced points and parallels.

topics.name: Constructing Tangents to a Circle
topics.description: Constructing a tangent at a point on a circle and the two tangents from an external point, using the circle-on-OA-as-diameter method and the angle-in-a-semicircle property.

learning_outcomes.description: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment (and perpendiculars to a line) and justify the steps using the equidistant-point property.
Bisect a given angle with ruler and compasses and justify the construction using the SSS congruence criterion.
Construct standard angles 60°, 120°, 30°, 90° and 45° (and combinations) using equilateral-triangle arcs and repeated bisection.
Construct triangles from SSS, SAS and ASA data and decide whether a triangle with given measurements is possible.
Construct a triangle given the base, a base angle and the sum or difference of the other two sides, and a right triangle given its hypotenuse and one side (RHS).

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Dividing a Segment in a Ratio
learning_outcomes.description: Divide a line segment internally in a given ratio m : n and justify the method by the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
Construct a triangle similar to a given triangle for a given scale factor, handling both reduction and enlargement.
Construct the tangent at a point of a circle and the two tangents from an external point, justifying the method with the angle-in-a-semicircle property.

chapter_summary.title: Constructions - Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This chapter shows how to draw accurate geometric figures using only a ruler and a pair of compasses. It covers bisecting segments and angles, building standard angles, constructing triangles from various data, dividing a segment in a ratio, making similar triangles to a scale factor, and drawing tangents to a circle - each with steps and a justification.

sections.heading: Bisecting segments and angles
bullets: To bisect a segment AB, draw equal arcs from A and from B on both sides and join their intersection points; the join is the perpendicular bisector and meets AB at its mid-point.
The construction works because the arc intersections are equidistant from A and B, and such points always lie on the perpendicular bisector.
To bisect an angle, cut an arc across both arms, then from those two points cut equal arcs meeting at R; the ray from the vertex through R is the bisector.
The angle-bisector construction is justified by SSS congruence of the two triangles formed.

sections.heading: Constructing standard angles
bullets: 60° is made by cutting an arc of the same radius twice, forming part of an equilateral triangle (each angle 60°).
120° is two 60° arcs placed side by side; 30° is the bisector of 60°; 45° is the bisector of 90°.
90° is obtained by bisecting the angle between the 60° and 120° positions, or by erecting a perpendicular.
Repeated bisection and addition give further angles such as 15°, 22.5°, 75° and 105°.

sections.heading: Constructing triangles
bullets: SSS: draw the base, then cut arcs of the other two side-lengths from the two ends to locate the third vertex.
SAS: draw the base, construct the given included angle, mark the second side, and join.
ASA: draw the base and construct the two base angles; the arms meet at the third vertex.
Special cases: given a base angle and the SUM or DIFFERENCE of the other two sides, use the perpendicular bisector of an auxiliary segment; RHS uses a perpendicular and an arc of the hypotenuse.

sections.heading: Dividing a segment and making similar triangles
bullets: To divide AB in ratio m : n, draw an acute ray from A, mark (m + n) equal parts, join the last point to B, and draw a parallel through the m-th point.
The division point is located by the Basic Proportionality (Thales) Theorem, which guarantees AP : PB = m : n.
A triangle similar to ABC with scale factor p/q uses the same equal-marks-and-parallel idea on a ray from a vertex.
If p > q the new triangle is larger (enlargement); if p < q it is smaller (reduction).

sections.heading: Constructing tangents to a circle
bullets: A tangent touches a circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
For a point on the circle, draw the radius and erect a perpendicular to it at that point.
From an external point A, draw the circle on OA as diameter; it cuts the given circle at the two points of contact P and Q.
Because an angle in a semicircle is 90°, AP and AQ are perpendicular to the radii and are the required tangents; they are equal in length.

key_takeaways: Ruler-and-compass constructions rely only on a straight edge and compasses; the protractor merely checks the result.
Equal arcs from the two ends of a segment give the perpendicular bisector; equal arcs on the arms of an angle give its bisector.
60° arises from an equilateral-triangle arc, and 30°, 45°, 90°, 120° follow by bisection, doubling and perpendiculars.
Triangles are built from SSS, SAS or ASA data, provided the triangle inequality (and angle sum) are satisfied.
The perpendicular-bisector trick handles a given sum or difference of two sides; the RHS case handles right triangles.
Dividing a segment in a ratio and constructing a similar triangle both rest on the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
Tangents from an external point are equal and are found using the circle on OA as diameter and the angle-in-a-semicircle property.

glossary.definition: An accurate geometric drawing made with only a ruler (straight edge) and compasses, following a definite sequence of justified steps.
The line that cuts a segment into two equal parts at right angles; every point on it is equidistant from the two ends of the segment.
A ray from the vertex of an angle that divides it into two equal angles.
To divide a segment or an angle into two equal parts.
Part of a circle drawn with compasses; intersecting arcs locate points used in constructions.
An angle such as 60°, 30°, 90° or 45° that can be constructed exactly with ruler and compasses.
Sets of data (three sides; two sides and the included angle; two angles and the included side) that determine a unique triangle.
The condition that the sum of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the third side; needed for an SSS triangle to exist.
Construction of a right triangle from its hypotenuse and one other side by erecting a perpendicular and cutting an arc equal to the hypotenuse.

glossary.term: Dividing a segment in a ratio
glossary.definition: Locating the point that splits a segment internally as m : n using an auxiliary ray of equal marks and a parallel line.
Thales theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio; it justifies the ratio and similarity constructions.
The ratio p/q of the sides of a constructed triangle to the corresponding sides of the given triangle; p > q enlarges, p < q reduces.
Triangles with equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides, having the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
A line that touches a circle at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.
The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle, which is always a right angle; used to justify the tangent construction.

worksheet.title: Worksheet - Constructions (NIOS Mathematics Class 10)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. For every construction, list the ordered steps of construction and give the justification where asked. Use a ruler and compasses only; a protractor may be used to verify.

questions.question: Write the steps of construction to draw the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB = 7 cm.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw AB = 7 cm. (2) With A as centre and radius more than half of AB (say 4 cm), draw arcs above and below AB. (3) With B as centre and the SAME radius, draw arcs cutting the first pair at P (above) and Q (below). (4) Join PQ; it meets AB at M. Then PQ is the perpendicular bisector and M is the mid-point (AM = MB = 3.5 cm). Justification: AP = BP = AQ = BQ, so P and Q are equidistant from A and B and lie on the perpendicular bisector.
questions.explanation: Standard perpendicular-bisector construction with justification.

questions.question: State the steps to bisect a given angle ABC, and name the congruence criterion used in the justification.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) With B as centre and any radius, draw an arc cutting BA at P and BC at Q. (2) With P as centre and radius more than half of PQ, draw an arc in the interior. (3) With Q as centre and the same radius, cut it at R. (4) Join BR; then angle ABR = angle RBC. Justification: BP = BQ and PR = QR (equal radii), BR common, so triangles BPR and BQR are congruent by SSS, giving equal angles at B.
questions.explanation: Angle bisector steps; SSS is the criterion.

questions.question: How is an angle of 60° constructed with ruler and compasses? Why does it measure exactly 60°?
questions.answer: Draw a ray BC. With B as centre and any radius draw an arc cutting BC at Q. With Q as centre and the same radius, cut the arc at R. Join BR; angle RBC = 60°. It is exactly 60° because BQ = QR = BR, forming an equilateral triangle, and every angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.
questions.explanation: Equilateral-arc method.

questions.question: Describe how to construct an angle of 45° starting from scratch.
questions.answer: First construct 90°: draw ray BC, mark 60° and 120° positions on an arc from B, and bisect the gap between them to get a 90° angle at B (or erect a perpendicular to BC at B). Then BISECT the 90° angle using the angle-bisector construction. Half of 90° is 45°, the required angle.
questions.explanation: 45° = bisect 90°.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct triangle ABC with BC = 6 cm, CA = 5 cm and AB = 4 cm (SSS).
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw base BC = 6 cm. (2) With B as centre and radius 4 cm (= AB), draw an arc. (3) With C as centre and radius 5 cm (= CA), draw an arc cutting the first at A. (4) Join AB and AC. Triangle ABC is the required triangle. The construction is possible because 4 + 5 > 6, 5 + 6 > 4 and 4 + 6 > 5 (triangle inequality).
questions.explanation: SSS construction; check triangle inequality.

questions.question: Construct triangle ABC in which BC = 5 cm, angle B = 60° and AB + AC = 8 cm. Give the steps and the justification.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw BC = 5 cm. (2) At B construct angle CBX = 60°. (3) Along BX mark BD = 8 cm (the sum AB + AC). (4) Join DC. (5) Draw the perpendicular bisector of DC; it meets BD at A. (6) Join AC. Triangle ABC is required. Justification: A lies on the perpendicular bisector of DC, so AD = AC. Then AB + AC = AB + AD = BD = 8 cm, and angle B = 60° as constructed.
questions.explanation: Sum-of-two-sides case using perpendicular bisector.

questions.question: Explain how to divide a line segment AB of length 8 cm in the ratio 3 : 2.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw AB = 8 cm. (2) Draw a ray AX making an acute angle with AB. (3) Mark 3 + 2 = 5 equal parts A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 on AX. (4) Join A5 to B. (5) Through A3 draw a line parallel to A5B meeting AB at P. Then AP : PB = 3 : 2. Justification: by the Basic Proportionality Theorem the parallel divides AB in the same ratio as the equal parts, i.e. 3 : 2.
questions.explanation: Ratio division via equal marks and a parallel.

questions.question: Construct a triangle similar to a given triangle ABC with scale factor 3/4. Write the steps.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw triangle ABC. (2) Below BC draw a ray BX making an acute angle with BC. (3) Mark 4 equal points B1, B2, B3, B4 on BX (take the larger of 3 and 4). (4) Join B4 to C. (5) Through B3 draw a line parallel to B4C meeting BC at C'. (6) Through C' draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at A'. Triangle A'BC' is similar to ABC with each side 3/4 of the original. Justification: by the Basic Proportionality Theorem BC' : BC = 3 : 4, and the parallel sides make the triangles similar (equal angles).
questions.explanation: Scale factor < 1 (reduction) using 4 marks.

questions.question: Construct the two tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm from a point A which is 7 cm from the centre O. State the steps and justify.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm; mark A with OA = 7 cm. (2) Find the mid-point M of OA (perpendicular bisector of OA). (3) With M as centre and radius MO, draw a circle; it cuts the given circle at P and Q. (4) Join AP and AQ - the two tangents. Justification: OA is a diameter of the new circle, so angle OPA = angle OQA = 90° (angle in a semicircle). Hence AP is perpendicular to radius OP and AQ to OQ, so both are tangents; also AP = AQ.
questions.explanation: External-point tangents via circle on OA as diameter.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct triangle PQR with QR = 6 cm, angle Q = 45° and angle R = 60° (ASA).
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Draw base QR = 6 cm. (2) At Q construct angle Q = 45°. (3) At R construct angle R = 60°. (4) The two arms meet at P. Triangle PQR is the required triangle. (The third angle P = 180° - 45° - 60° = 75°, which can be used to check the drawing.)
questions.explanation: ASA construction.

questions.question: The instruments allowed in a ruler-and-compass construction are
questions.answer: ruler and compasses
questions.explanation: Only a straight edge and compasses are used; a protractor merely checks.

questions.question: To bisect a segment AB, the arcs from A and from B must be drawn with
options: radius less than half of AB
the same radius, more than half of AB
questions.answer: the same radius, more than half of AB
questions.explanation: Equal radii greater than half AB make the arcs intersect on both sides.

questions.question: The line joining the two arc intersections in the segment-bisecting construction is the
questions.answer: perpendicular bisector
questions.explanation: It cuts AB at right angles through the mid-point.

questions.question: Points P and Q used to bisect AB are chosen so that each is
questions.answer: equidistant from A and B
questions.explanation: Equal radii make AP = BP and AQ = BQ, so P, Q lie on the perpendicular bisector.

questions.question: If AB = 10 cm is bisected, the distance of the mid-point M from A is
questions.answer: 5 cm
questions.explanation: The mid-point divides AB into two equal 5 cm halves.

questions.question: The perpendicular bisector of AB makes an angle with AB of
questions.explanation: By definition it is perpendicular to AB.

questions.question: To drop a perpendicular from an external point to a line, one first draws
options: an arc from the point cutting the line at two points
questions.answer: an arc from the point cutting the line at two points
questions.explanation: Those two points are then used like the ends of a segment to find the foot of the perpendicular.

questions.question: A protractor in these constructions is used to
questions.answer: verify the constructed figure
questions.explanation: The construction itself must use only ruler and compasses.

questions.question: If the two arcs in the bisector construction are drawn with radius exactly half of AB, they will
options: just touch at the mid-point (no clear intersection)
questions.answer: just touch at the mid-point (no clear intersection)
questions.explanation: The radius must exceed half of AB for two distinct intersection points.

questions.question: An angle bisector divides an angle into
questions.answer: two equal parts
questions.explanation: Bisect means divide into two equal parts.

questions.question: In bisecting angle ABC, the first arc from B cuts the arms BA and BC at
questions.answer: two points P and Q
questions.explanation: The arc meets each arm once, giving P on BA and Q on BC.

questions.question: The congruence criterion that justifies the angle-bisector construction is
questions.answer: SSS
questions.explanation: Triangles BPR and BQR have three pairs of equal sides.

questions.question: Bisecting a 90° angle produces two angles of
questions.explanation: Half of 90° is 45°.

questions.question: Bisecting a 60° angle produces two angles of
questions.explanation: Half of 60° is 30°.

questions.question: To construct a 15° angle by bisection alone, you would bisect
options: a 30° angle (which itself is a bisected 60°)
questions.answer: a 30° angle (which itself is a bisected 60°)
questions.explanation: 60° -> 30° -> 15° by two bisections.

questions.question: After joining B to R, the equality angle PBR = angle QBR follows because
options: triangles BPR and BQR are congruent
questions.answer: triangles BPR and BQR are congruent
questions.explanation: SSS congruence gives the equal angles at B.

questions.question: For step 2 and 3 of the angle bisection, the radius used from P and Q must be
questions.answer: more than half of PQ
questions.explanation: So the two arcs meet at an interior point R.

questions.question: The angle constructed directly from a single equilateral-triangle arc is
questions.explanation: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.

questions.question: An angle of 120° is constructed by
options: placing two 60° arcs side by side
questions.answer: placing two 60° arcs side by side

questions.question: A 30° angle is obtained by bisecting
questions.explanation: Half of 60° is 30°.

questions.question: A 45° angle is obtained by bisecting
questions.explanation: Half of 90° is 45°.

questions.question: A 75° angle can be constructed as
questions.answer: the bisector of the 60°-90° gap
questions.explanation: The midpoint between 60° and 90° is 75°.

questions.question: An angle of 105° equals
questions.explanation: 105° = 60° + 45° using constructed 60° and 45°.

questions.question: The reason a compass arc of the same radius gives 60° is that it creates
questions.answer: an equilateral triangle
questions.explanation: Equal radii make all three sides equal.

questions.question: Bisecting a 45° angle gives
questions.explanation: Half of 45° is 22.5°.

questions.question: Which angle CANNOT be constructed by ruler and compasses using only 60° arcs and bisection?
questions.explanation: 40° is not a multiple obtainable by bisecting/adding 60° (it needs trisection).

questions.question: To construct 90° one convenient method is to
questions.answer: bisect the 60°-to-120° gap
questions.explanation: The bisector of that gap stands at 90° from the base.

questions.question: An angle of 90° is also called a
questions.answer: right angle
questions.explanation: 90° is a right angle.

questions.question: To construct a triangle from three given sides, the case is called
questions.answer: SSS
questions.explanation: Three sides given.

questions.question: A triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm
questions.answer: cannot be constructed
questions.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 < 8, so the triangle inequality fails.

questions.question: A triangle with sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm
questions.answer: can be constructed
questions.explanation: Every pair of sides sums to more than the third.

questions.question: In the SAS case the given angle must be the one
options: included between the two given sides
questions.answer: included between the two given sides
questions.explanation: SAS = two sides and the INCLUDED angle.

questions.question: In the ASA case the given side is the one
options: included between the two given angles
questions.answer: included between the two given angles
questions.explanation: ASA = two angles and the INCLUDED side.

questions.question: If two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°, the third angle (needed before an ASA construction) is
In the SSS construction, the third vertex is located as the
questions.answer: intersection of two arcs
questions.explanation: Arcs of the two side-lengths from the base ends meet at the vertex.

questions.question: For an SAS construction of triangle ABC with BC = 5 cm, angle B = 60°, AB = 4 cm, the first step is to
options: mark AB = 4 cm in the air
draw an arc of radius 4 cm
questions.answer: draw the base BC = 5 cm
questions.explanation: The base is drawn first, then the angle at B.

questions.question: Which set of data does NOT in general fix a unique triangle?
options: SSA (two sides and a non-included angle)
questions.answer: SSA (two sides and a non-included angle)
questions.explanation: SSA can give two different triangles (ambiguous case).

questions.question: The condition sum of any two sides > third side is called the
questions.answer: triangle inequality
questions.explanation: It decides whether an SSS triangle can exist.

questions.question: To construct an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm, you draw a 6 cm base and cut arcs of radius
questions.answer: 6 cm from each end
questions.explanation: All sides equal 6 cm, so both arcs have radius 6 cm.

questions.question: When the base, a base angle and the SUM of the other two sides are given, the key auxiliary construction is the
options: perpendicular bisector of an auxiliary segment
questions.answer: perpendicular bisector of an auxiliary segment
questions.explanation: It makes AD = AC so that AB + AC = BD.

questions.question: In constructing ABC given BC, angle B and AB + AC = s, point D is marked so that BD equals
questions.answer: AB + AC = s
questions.explanation: BD is the full sum along the arm of the angle.

questions.question: The perpendicular bisector of DC meets BD at A because at A
questions.answer: AD = AC
questions.explanation: A on the perpendicular bisector of DC is equidistant from D and C.

questions.question: When the DIFFERENCE AB - AC is given (AB longer), the mark BD along the arm equals
questions.answer: AB - AC
questions.explanation: BD is the given difference.

questions.question: The RHS construction is used to build a
options: right triangle from hypotenuse and one side
questions.answer: right triangle from hypotenuse and one side
questions.explanation: RHS = Right angle, Hypotenuse, Side.

questions.question: In an RHS construction with right angle at B, after drawing BC and the perpendicular at B, the vertex A is found by drawing an arc from C of radius equal to
questions.answer: the hypotenuse AC
questions.explanation: The arc of the hypotenuse cuts the perpendicular at A.

questions.question: A right triangle has one leg 6 cm and hypotenuse 10 cm. The other leg (to verify the construction) is
questions.answer: 8 cm
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras, sqrt(10^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(64) = 8 cm.

questions.question: For the sum-of-sides case to give a valid triangle, the sum AB + AC must be
questions.answer: greater than BC
questions.explanation: Two sides together must exceed the base (triangle inequality).

questions.question: In the difference case, if AC - AB is given instead, the point D is taken
options: on the arm produced beyond B
questions.answer: on the arm produced beyond B
questions.explanation: The difference is laid off in the opposite sense along the arm.

questions.question: The right angle in the RHS construction is made by
options: erecting a perpendicular to BC at B
questions.answer: erecting a perpendicular to BC at B
questions.explanation: A perpendicular gives the 90° at B.

questions.question: To divide AB in ratio m : n, the number of equal parts marked on the auxiliary ray is
questions.answer: m + n
questions.explanation: You need m + n equal divisions.

questions.question: To divide a segment in ratio 3 : 4, how many equal points are marked on the ray?
questions.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts.

questions.question: After marking the equal parts, the LAST point is joined to
questions.answer: B
questions.explanation: Join the (m+n)-th point to B, then draw a parallel through the m-th point.

questions.question: The theorem that justifies dividing a segment in a given ratio is the
questions.answer: Basic Proportionality (Thales) Theorem
questions.explanation: Parallel lines cut the sides proportionally.

questions.question: To divide AB in ratio 2 : 3, the parallel to the last-point-B line is drawn through the
questions.answer: 2nd point from A
questions.explanation: The parallel goes through the m-th (= 2nd) point.

questions.question: The ray AX drawn from A for the ratio construction must make with AB an
questions.answer: acute angle
questions.explanation: Any convenient acute angle is used.

questions.question: If AB = 12 cm is divided in ratio 1 : 2, then AP equals
questions.answer: 4 cm
questions.explanation: AP : PB = 1 : 2 means AP = 12 x 1/3 = 4 cm.

questions.question: The equal parts on the auxiliary ray are marked using
options: a fixed compass opening stepped along the ray
questions.answer: a fixed compass opening stepped along the ray
questions.explanation: A fixed opening guarantees equal spacing.

questions.question: The parallel line in the construction works because equal intercepts on one transversal make
options: equal intercepts on the other line
questions.answer: equal intercepts on the other line
questions.explanation: Basic Proportionality Theorem with equal parts gives proportional division.

questions.question: A scale factor of 3/4 produces a triangle that is
questions.answer: smaller than the original
questions.explanation: p/q < 1 means reduction.

questions.question: A scale factor of 5/3 produces a triangle that is
questions.answer: larger than the original
questions.explanation: p/q > 1 means enlargement.

questions.question: For scale factor 2/3, the number of equal points marked on the ray from B is
questions.explanation: Mark the larger of 2 and 3, i.e. 3 points.

questions.question: For scale factor 5/3, the number of equal points marked on the ray is
questions.explanation: Mark the larger of 5 and 3, i.e. 5 points.

questions.question: In the similar-triangle construction, after marking points, you first join to C the point
questions.answer: the q-th point (denominator)
questions.explanation: Join Bq (the q-th point) to C, then draw a parallel through Bp.

questions.question: The sides of the new triangle are made proportional to the original using lines that are
questions.answer: parallel to the original sides
questions.explanation: Parallels create similar triangles by the BPT.

questions.question: If a triangle has sides 6, 8, 10 cm and scale factor 1/2, the new sides are
questions.explanation: Each side halved.

questions.question: For scale factor 7/5 the point through which the parallel to B5C is drawn is
questions.answer: B7
questions.explanation: The parallel goes through the p-th (= 7th) point, meeting BC produced.

questions.question: When the scale factor exceeds 1, the parallel meets
questions.answer: BC produced (extended)
questions.explanation: Enlargement pushes C' beyond C on BC produced.

questions.question: Two similar triangles have
options: equal corresponding angles and proportional sides
questions.answer: equal corresponding angles and proportional sides
questions.explanation: Definition of similar triangles.

questions.question: A tangent to a circle touches it at
questions.answer: exactly one point
questions.explanation: A tangent meets the circle at a single point of contact.

questions.question: A tangent is always ____ to the radius at the point of contact.
questions.answer: perpendicular
questions.explanation: Radius meets tangent at 90°.

questions.question: From a point outside a circle, the number of tangents that can be drawn is
questions.explanation: Exactly two tangents from an external point.

questions.question: From a point ON the circle, the number of tangents is
questions.explanation: Exactly one tangent at a point of the circle.

questions.question: In the external-point construction, the auxiliary circle is drawn on OA as
questions.answer: a diameter
questions.explanation: OA is the diameter of the new circle.

questions.question: The auxiliary circle passes through P (a contact point) so that angle OPA equals 90° because
options: of the angle in a semicircle
questions.answer: of the angle in a semicircle
questions.explanation: OA is a diameter, so the angle it subtends at P is 90°.

questions.question: The two tangents drawn from an external point are always
questions.answer: equal in length
questions.explanation: Tangents from an external point are equal.

questions.question: In ruler-and-compass constructions a protractor is used only to check the figure, not to construct it.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The construction must use ruler and compasses only.

questions.question: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equidistant from A and B.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: That is the defining property of the perpendicular bisector.

questions.question: The angle-bisector construction is justified by the SSS congruence criterion.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Triangles BPR and BQR are congruent by SSS.

questions.question: An angle of 60° is constructed by cutting an arc of the same radius twice.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: This forms an equilateral triangle giving 60°.

questions.question: A 40° angle can be constructed exactly with ruler and compasses.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: 40° would require trisecting 120°, which is not possible with ruler and compasses.

questions.question: A triangle with sides 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm can be constructed.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: 2 + 3 = 5 < 6 violates the triangle inequality.

questions.question: In the sum-of-sides construction, the perpendicular bisector of DC makes AD = AC.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: A on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from D and C.

questions.question: To divide a segment in ratio m : n you mark m + n equal parts on an auxiliary ray.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: You need m + n equal divisions.

questions.question: A scale factor greater than 1 produces a smaller triangle.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges the triangle.

questions.question: The two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Tangents from an external point are always equal.

questions.question: The line that divides a segment into two equal parts at right angles is its ____.
questions.answer: perpendicular bisector
questions.explanation: It passes through the mid-point at 90°.

questions.question: To bisect AB the arcs from A and B are drawn with radius ____ than half of AB.
questions.answer: more
questions.explanation: The radius must exceed half of AB.

questions.question: A ray that divides an angle into two equal angles is called the ____.
questions.answer: angle bisector
questions.explanation: It halves the angle.

questions.question: Bisecting a 90° angle gives two angles of ____ degrees each.
questions.explanation: Half of 90 is 45.

questions.question: An equilateral-triangle arc gives an angle of ____ degrees.
questions.explanation: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.

questions.question: An angle of 120° is made by placing ____ 60° arcs side by side.
questions.answer: two

questions.question: A 75° angle is the bisector of the gap between 60° and ____ degrees.
questions.explanation: The midpoint of 60 and 90 is 75.

questions.question: A triangle can be drawn from three sides only if the sum of any two sides is ____ than the third.
questions.answer: greater
questions.explanation: This is the triangle inequality.

questions.question: Constructing a triangle from two angles and the included side is the ____ case.
questions.answer: ASA
questions.explanation: Angle-Side-Angle.

questions.question: In the sum-of-sides construction, along the arm we mark BD equal to the ____ of the two unknown sides.
questions.answer: sum
questions.explanation: BD = AB + AC.

questions.question: A right triangle can be constructed from its hypotenuse and one side by the ____ case.
questions.answer: RHS
questions.explanation: Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side.

questions.question: To divide a segment in ratio 4 : 3, mark ____ equal parts on the ray.
Dividing a segment in a ratio is justified by the ____ Theorem.
questions.answer: Basic Proportionality
questions.explanation: Also called Thales theorem.

questions.question: For a similar triangle with scale factor 3/5, mark ____ equal points on the auxiliary ray.
questions.explanation: Mark the larger of 3 and 5, i.e. 5 points.

questions.question: A tangent is ____ to the radius at the point of contact.
questions.answer: perpendicular
questions.explanation: Radius meets tangent at 90°.

questions.question: List the steps to draw the perpendicular bisector of a segment PQ.
questions.answer: (1) With P as centre and radius more than half PQ, draw arcs on both sides. (2) With Q as centre and the same radius, draw arcs cutting the first at X and Y. (3) Join XY; it meets PQ at its mid-point M and is perpendicular to PQ.
questions.explanation: Standard perpendicular-bisector steps.

questions.question: Why must the compass radius be more than half the segment when bisecting it?
questions.answer: If the radius were less than half the segment, the arcs from the two ends would not reach each other and would not intersect. A radius more than half ensures the arcs from both ends overlap and cross at two points, one on each side of the segment, which are then joined to form the perpendicular bisector.
questions.explanation: Arcs must overlap to intersect.

questions.question: Describe how to draw a perpendicular to a line l at a given point P on it.
questions.answer: (1) With P as centre and any radius, cut the line at two points A and B (one on each side of P). (2) With A and B as centres and equal radii more than half of AB, draw arcs meeting at C above the line. (3) Join PC; PC is perpendicular to l at P.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular at a point using equal arcs.

questions.question: Write the steps to bisect angle XYZ.
questions.answer: (1) With Y as centre and any radius, draw an arc cutting YX at P and YZ at Q. (2) With P and Q as centres and equal radii more than half PQ, draw arcs meeting at R. (3) Join YR; then YR bisects angle XYZ.
questions.explanation: Angle-bisector steps.

questions.question: Prove that the ray YR constructed above bisects angle XYZ.
questions.answer: In triangles YPR and YQR: YP = YQ (equal radii of the first arc), PR = QR (equal radii of the second pair of arcs), and YR is common. By the SSS criterion triangle YPR is congruent to triangle YQR. Corresponding angles are equal, so angle PYR = angle QYR, i.e. angle XYR = angle ZYR. Hence YR bisects the angle.
questions.explanation: SSS congruence justification.

questions.question: How do you construct a 30° angle?
questions.answer: First construct a 60° angle using the equilateral-triangle arc (cut an arc of the same radius twice from the vertex). Then bisect the 60° angle using the angle-bisector construction. Each half is 30°.
questions.explanation: 30° = bisected 60°.

questions.question: Explain how to construct a 90° angle at a point B on a line.
questions.answer: With B as centre draw an arc cutting the line at Q. From Q, with the same radius, cut the arc at R (that gives 60°). From R, again with the same radius, cut the arc at S (that gives 120°). Bisect the angle between R and S; the bisector stands at 90° to the line at B. (Equivalently, erect a perpendicular to the line at B.)
questions.explanation: 90° via bisecting 60°-120° gap.

questions.question: Describe how to construct an angle of 105°.
questions.answer: 105° = 60° + 45°. (1) Construct a 60° angle at the vertex using an equilateral-triangle arc. (2) Construct a 90° angle (bisect the 60°-120° gap) and then bisect it to get 45°, positioned adjacent to the 60°. Adding the 45° onto the 60° arm gives a total of 105°. Alternatively, construct 90° and 120° and bisect the 90°-120° gap to get 105° directly.

questions.question: Why can an angle of 60° be constructed but an angle of 20° cannot, with ruler and compasses?
questions.answer: 60° comes from an equilateral triangle, which ruler and compasses can build directly. Getting 20° would require TRISECTING the 60° angle into three equal parts. Trisection of a general angle is impossible with ruler and compasses (a classical result), so 20° cannot be constructed exactly, whereas 30° (a bisection of 60°) can.
questions.explanation: Trisection is impossible; bisection is possible.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct triangle ABC with BC = 5 cm, CA = 4 cm, AB = 6 cm.
questions.answer: (1) Draw base BC = 5 cm. (2) With B as centre and radius 6 cm (AB), draw an arc. (3) With C as centre and radius 4 cm (CA), draw an arc cutting the first at A. (4) Join AB and AC. Triangle ABC is complete (valid since 5 + 4 > 6 etc.).
questions.explanation: SSS construction.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct triangle ABC with BC = 6 cm, angle B = 45° and AB = 5 cm (SAS).
questions.answer: (1) Draw base BC = 6 cm. (2) At B construct a 45° angle (construct 90° and bisect it) to get ray BX. (3) Along BX mark BA = 5 cm. (4) Join AC. Triangle ABC is the required triangle.
questions.explanation: SAS construction with 45°.

questions.question: Is it possible to construct a triangle with sides 4 cm, 4 cm and 9 cm? Justify.
questions.answer: No. For a triangle to exist, the sum of any two sides must exceed the third. Here 4 + 4 = 8, which is LESS than 9. The two short sides cannot reach across the 9 cm base, so the arcs of radius 4 cm from each end of the base do not meet. The triangle cannot be constructed.
questions.explanation: Triangle inequality fails.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct triangle ABC with BC = 7 cm, angle B = 60° and angle C = 45° (ASA).
questions.answer: (1) Draw base BC = 7 cm. (2) At B construct a 60° angle. (3) At C construct a 45° angle. (4) The arms of these two angles meet at A. Triangle ABC is complete. (Check: angle A = 180 - 60 - 45 = 75°.)
questions.explanation: ASA construction.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are 70° and 40° and the side between the 70° angle and the third vertex is 5 cm. Explain how you would construct it.
questions.answer: The side given (5 cm) is NOT between the two given angles, so this is not directly ASA. First find the third angle: 180 - 70 - 40 = 70°. Now the 5 cm side lies between the 40° angle and the 70° (third) angle, so we can apply ASA with those two angles at the ends of the 5 cm base. Steps: draw base = 5 cm; at one end construct 40°, at the other construct 70°; the arms meet at the third vertex.
questions.explanation: Use angle sum, then ASA.

questions.question: Construct triangle ABC with BC = 6 cm, angle B = 60° and AB - AC = 2 cm (AB longer). Give steps and justification.
questions.answer: (1) Draw BC = 6 cm. (2) At B construct angle CBX = 60°. (3) Along BX mark BD = 2 cm (= AB - AC). (4) Join DC. (5) Draw the perpendicular bisector of DC; it meets ray BX (beyond D) at A. (6) Join AC. Justification: A lies on the perpendicular bisector of DC so AD = AC. Then AB - AC = AB - AD = BD = 2 cm, and angle B = 60° as required.
questions.explanation: Difference-of-sides case.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct a right triangle with the right angle at B, BC = 4 cm and hypotenuse AC = 5 cm (RHS).
questions.answer: (1) Draw BC = 4 cm. (2) At B erect a perpendicular to BC. (3) With C as centre and radius 5 cm (the hypotenuse), draw an arc cutting the perpendicular at A. (4) Join AC. Then angle B = 90° and AC = 5 cm. (Check: AB = 3 cm by Pythagoras.)
questions.explanation: RHS construction.

questions.question: In the sum-of-two-sides construction, why does A lie on the perpendicular bisector of DC?
questions.answer: We need AD = AC so that AB + AC = AB + AD = BD (the given sum). Any point equidistant from D and C lies on the perpendicular bisector of DC. Choosing A as the intersection of that perpendicular bisector with the arm BD guarantees AD = AC, which makes AB + AC equal to the marked length BD.
questions.explanation: Equidistant property gives AD = AC.

questions.question: A right triangle is to be constructed with hypotenuse 13 cm and one side 5 cm. What is the length of the third side, and how is the right angle drawn?
questions.answer: The third side = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. The right angle is drawn by erecting a perpendicular to the known 5 cm side at its end, then cutting an arc of 13 cm (the hypotenuse) from the far end to locate the third vertex.
questions.explanation: Pythagoras gives 12 cm; perpendicular for the right angle.

questions.question: Write the steps to divide a segment AB in the ratio 2 : 3.
questions.answer: (1) Draw AB. (2) Draw ray AX at an acute angle to AB. (3) Mark 2 + 3 = 5 equal points A1..A5 on AX. (4) Join A5 to B. (5) Through A2 draw a line parallel to A5B meeting AB at P. Then AP : PB = 2 : 3.
questions.explanation: Ratio 2:3 division.

questions.question: State and explain the theorem used to justify dividing a segment in a given ratio.
questions.answer: The Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem): if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, it divides those two sides in the same ratio. In the construction, the equal marks make one transversal have equal parts, and the parallel line then cuts AB in the same ratio m : n, giving AP : PB = m : n.
questions.explanation: BPT / Thales justification.

questions.question: AB = 9 cm is divided in ratio 1 : 2 at P. Find AP and PB.
questions.answer: Total parts = 1 + 2 = 3. Each part = 9/3 = 3 cm. AP = 1 part = 3 cm; PB = 2 parts = 6 cm. So AP = 3 cm and PB = 6 cm.
questions.explanation: Split 9 cm as 3 cm : 6 cm.

questions.question: Explain, with steps, how to construct a point P on AB (= 10 cm) such that AP : PB = 3 : 2, and find AP.
questions.answer: Steps: draw AB = 10 cm; draw ray AX at an acute angle; mark 5 equal points on AX; join the 5th point to B; through the 3rd point draw a parallel to that line meeting AB at P. Then AP : PB = 3 : 2. Length: total parts 5, each 10/5 = 2 cm, so AP = 3 x 2 = 6 cm and PB = 4 cm.
questions.explanation: 3:2 of 10 cm gives AP = 6 cm.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct a triangle similar to triangle ABC with scale factor 2/3.
questions.answer: (1) Draw triangle ABC. (2) Below BC draw ray BX at an acute angle. (3) Mark 3 equal points B1, B2, B3 on BX. (4) Join B3 to C. (5) Through B2 draw a line parallel to B3C meeting BC at C'. (6) Through C' draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at A'. Triangle A'BC' has each side 2/3 of the corresponding side of ABC.
questions.explanation: Reduction scale factor 2/3.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct a triangle similar to triangle ABC with scale factor 4/3 (enlargement).
questions.answer: (1) Draw triangle ABC. (2) Below BC draw ray BX at an acute angle. (3) Mark 4 equal points B1..B4 (the larger of 4 and 3). (4) Join B3 (the 3rd point) to C. (5) Through B4 draw a line parallel to B3C meeting BC PRODUCED at C'. (6) Through C' draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA produced at A'. Triangle A'BC' has each side 4/3 of ABC.
questions.explanation: Enlargement scale factor 4/3; C' on BC produced.

questions.question: Why are the new and original triangles similar in the scale-factor construction?
questions.answer: The construction draws C'A' parallel to CA. A line parallel to one side of a triangle creates a smaller (or larger) triangle in which all three corresponding angles are equal (equal angles from parallel lines). Equal corresponding angles mean the triangles are similar (AA similarity), and the equal-marks arrangement fixes the ratio of the sides to the chosen scale factor.
questions.explanation: Parallel side gives equal angles -> AA similarity.

questions.question: How do you construct a tangent to a circle at a point P on it?
questions.answer: Join the centre O to the point P (the radius OP). Then construct a line perpendicular to OP at P (erect a perpendicular at P). This perpendicular is the required tangent, since the tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.
questions.explanation: Tangent perpendicular to radius.

questions.question: Write the steps to construct two tangents from an external point A to a circle with centre O, and justify the method.
questions.answer: (1) Join OA. (2) Find its mid-point M by drawing the perpendicular bisector of OA. (3) With M as centre and radius MO (= MA) draw a circle; it cuts the given circle at P and Q. (4) Join AP and AQ - the two tangents. Justification: OA is a diameter of the new circle, so angle OPA = angle OQA = 90° (angle in a semicircle). Thus AP is perpendicular to radius OP and AQ to OQ, so both AP and AQ are tangents to the circle. Also AP = AQ.
questions.explanation: External-point tangent construction with justification.

questions.question: A point A is 10 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 6 cm. Find the length of the tangent from A.
questions.answer: The tangent, the radius to the contact point, and the line OA form a right triangle with the right angle at the contact point. Tangent length = sqrt(OA^2 - r^2) = sqrt(10^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(100 - 36) = sqrt(64) = 8 cm.
questions.explanation: Tangent length = sqrt(100-36) = 8 cm.

questions.question: Why is the mid-point of OA used when drawing tangents from an external point A?
questions.answer: The mid-point M of OA is the centre of the auxiliary circle drawn on OA as diameter. Making OA a diameter forces any point where this circle meets the given circle to see OA at a right angle (angle in a semicircle). Those right angles are exactly what make AP and AQ perpendicular to the radii, i.e. tangents. So M must be the mid-point so that OA becomes a proper diameter.
questions.explanation: Mid-point makes OA the diameter of the helper circle.

questions.question: How would you construct an angle of 120° at a point B on a line?
questions.answer: With B as centre draw an arc cutting the line at Q. From Q, with the same radius, cut the arc at R (this fixes 60°). From R, with the same radius again, cut the arc at S. Join BS; angle SBC = 120°. It is two 60° arcs placed side by side (60° + 60° = 120°).
questions.explanation: 120° = two equilateral arcs.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A carpenter wants to find the exact middle of a wooden strip AB = 12 cm and cut it at right angles.

(i) Name the construction he should use.
(ii) List the steps.
(iii) Where is the mid-point located?
(iv) State the length from A to the mid-point.
questions.answer: (i) The perpendicular-bisector construction. (ii) Steps: draw AB = 12 cm; with A as centre and radius more than 6 cm draw arcs above and below; with B as centre and the same radius draw arcs cutting them at P and Q; join PQ. (iii) The mid-point M is where PQ crosses AB. (iv) AM = 6 cm (half of 12 cm).
questions.explanation: Perpendicular bisector locates the mid-point at 6 cm.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A student has drawn angle ABC = 80° and wishes to split it into two equal angles.

(i) What construction is needed?
(ii) List the steps.
(iii) What is the measure of each half?
(iv) Which congruence rule justifies the equality of the two halves?
questions.answer: (i) The angle-bisector construction. (ii) With B as centre draw an arc cutting BA at P and BC at Q; with P and Q as centres and equal radii draw arcs meeting at R; join BR. (iii) Each half = 80/2 = 40°. (iv) SSS congruence (triangles BPR and BQR).
questions.explanation: Angle bisector; halves of 40°; SSS.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Standard angles are built from a basic 60° arc and by bisection.

(i) How is 60° constructed?
(ii) How is 30° obtained from it?
(iii) How is 90° constructed?
(iv) How is 45° obtained?
questions.answer: (i) 60° from an equilateral-triangle arc: cut an arc of the same radius twice from the vertex. (ii) 30° by bisecting the 60° angle. (iii) 90° by marking 60° and 120° on the arc and bisecting the gap between them (or by erecting a perpendicular). (iv) 45° by bisecting the 90° angle.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A triangle is to be built with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm.

(i) Which construction case is this?
(ii) Is the triangle possible? Justify.
(iii) List the steps.
(iv) Which side is drawn first?
questions.answer: (i) The SSS case (three sides given). (ii) Possible: 6 + 8 > 5, 6 + 5 > 8 and 8 + 5 > 6, so the triangle inequality holds. (iii) Draw the base (say 8 cm); from one end draw an arc of 6 cm and from the other an arc of 5 cm; their intersection is the third vertex; join it to both ends. (iv) The base (any chosen side, here 8 cm) is drawn first.
questions.explanation: SSS, valid by triangle inequality.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Construct triangle ABC given BC = 5 cm, angle B = 60° and AB + AC = 9 cm.

(i) What auxiliary length is marked along the arm of angle B?
(ii) What line is then drawn to locate A?
(iii) Why does AB + AC equal 9 cm in the result?
(iv) What must be true of 9 cm and 5 cm for a triangle to exist?
questions.answer: (i) Mark BD = 9 cm (the sum AB + AC) along the arm of the 60° angle. (ii) Join DC and draw the perpendicular bisector of DC; it meets BD at A. (iii) A lies on the perpendicular bisector of DC, so AD = AC; then AB + AC = AB + AD = BD = 9 cm. (iv) The sum 9 cm must be greater than the base 5 cm (triangle inequality), which it is.
questions.explanation: Sum-of-sides construction reasoning.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A right triangle is to be constructed with the right angle at B, side BC = 8 cm and hypotenuse AC = 17 cm.

(i) Name the construction case.
(ii) How is the right angle at B produced?
(iii) How is vertex A located?
(iv) Find the third side AB.
questions.answer: (i) The RHS case (right angle, hypotenuse, one side). (ii) Erect a perpendicular to BC at B. (iii) With C as centre and radius 17 cm (the hypotenuse) draw an arc cutting the perpendicular at A. (iv) AB = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(289 - 64) = sqrt(225) = 15 cm.
questions.explanation: RHS; AB = 15 cm by Pythagoras.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A segment AB = 14 cm is to be divided in the ratio 3 : 4.

(i) How many equal parts are marked on the auxiliary ray?
(ii) Through which point is the parallel drawn?
(iii) Which theorem justifies the method?
(iv) Find AP and PB.
questions.answer: (i) 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts. (ii) Through the 3rd point (Am with m = 3), draw a parallel to the line joining the 7th point to B. (iii) The Basic Proportionality (Thales) Theorem. (iv) Each part = 14/7 = 2 cm; AP = 3 x 2 = 6 cm, PB = 4 x 2 = 8 cm.
questions.explanation: Ratio 3:4 of 14 cm gives 6 cm and 8 cm.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Triangle ABC has sides 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm. A similar triangle is required with scale factor 3/2.

(i) Is the new triangle larger or smaller?
(ii) How many equal points are marked on the auxiliary ray?
(iii) The parallel through which point meets BC produced?
(iv) Find the sides of the new triangle.
questions.answer: (i) Larger, because 3/2 > 1 (enlargement). (ii) Mark the larger of 3 and 2, i.e. 3 equal points. (iii) Join the 2nd point to C, then through the 3rd point draw a parallel to that line meeting BC produced at C'. (iv) New sides = 3/2 of 4, 5, 6 = 6 cm, 7.5 cm, 9 cm.
questions.explanation: Enlargement 3/2; sides 6, 7.5, 9 cm.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Tangents are to be drawn from a point A, 10 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 6 cm.

(i) What auxiliary circle is drawn?
(ii) Why do the tangents touch the given circle at right angles to the radii?
(iii) How many tangents are there and are they equal?
(iv) Find the length of each tangent.
questions.answer: (i) A circle on OA as diameter (centre at the mid-point M of OA, radius MO). (ii) OA is a diameter of the auxiliary circle, so the angle it subtends at each intersection point P, Q is 90° (angle in a semicircle); hence AP is perpendicular to OP and AQ to OQ. (iii) There are two tangents and they are equal in length. (iv) Length = sqrt(10^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(64) = 8 cm.
questions.explanation: External tangents; each 8 cm long.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A point P lies on a circle with centre O.

(i) How many tangents can be drawn at P?
(ii) Describe the construction of the tangent at P.
(iii) What is the angle between the tangent and OP?
(iv) If a second point Q also lies on the circle, are the tangents at P and Q generally parallel?
questions.answer: (i) Exactly one tangent at a point on the circle. (ii) Join OP and erect a perpendicular to OP at P; that perpendicular is the tangent. (iii) 90° - the tangent is perpendicular to the radius OP. (iv) Not in general; they are parallel only when P and Q are the ends of a diameter, otherwise they meet when produced.
questions.explanation: Tangent at a point; perpendicular to radius.
